requirements: State-driven canonical index catch-up with daemon shutdown ownership
sourceAssessment: Adapter awaits each existing index.sync step serially until status.complete; removes only20-second/512-step catch-up abandonment. Native step canonical/network/deployment/storage/revision checks and bounded transaction/page work remain unchanged.
The production index exposes sync:step, and the owned wrapper preserves that contract. Native failures propagate directly without adapter retry; no partial publication is inferred.

Daemon supplies its existing stopping closure. While catch-up is incomplete, shutdown is checked before each subsequent step; an in-flight native step remains owned until it settles. Existing worker stopping checks prevent model/signing jobs after shutdown.
No wallet journal, submission, receipt reconciliation, model isolation or replay policy changed. Legacy non-Rolling signer composition is unchanged.

meaningfulCases: 600 finite native index steps complete beyond old cap
unfinished index shutdown after3steps performs no evaluation or broadcast
first exact native error is propagated after one step
existing final guarded query rejects changed revision/unavailable query before model/signing

limitations: Tests use labelled component fixtures; no live model/proof/chain/service operation performed.
Shutdown is cooperative between native steps; this change does not abort an in-flight RPC or change its existing transport boundary.
The old whole-initial-sync fixture was correctly replaced with state-driven shutdown, not treated as a required elapsed-time failure. Parent first cancelled obsolete-fixture run is not a pass claim.
